title: Is there an audience for this stuff?
author: broncos4thewin
selftext:
I feel like the answer is yes, but as someone completely new to this I don’t know how to find them, and I’m fearful of all the AI hate.

As a reasonably serious hobby filmmaker I know there are AI filmmakers who’ve attracted a serious audience on YouTube - it doesn’t interest me personally and almost everyone involved in film I know hates it, but there’s still clearly a lot of people who don’t care it’s AI and just want to watch it.

To be clear, I’m 90% just doing this for fun (currently vibe coding a retro point and click 80s babysitter/slasher game and having a blast) and certainly not for money, but I do feel it would be nice for some people to at least be able to play it and hopefully enjoy it.

I just don’t know the games scene at all. If you upload an AI game to itch.io is everyone just going to scream AI hate at you? Or is there some way to find people who are happy just to play the game if it’s fun and the story’s good? Like…AI filmmakers *have* found a niche so presumably it shouldn’t be impossible for gaming either.

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body:
Is there an audience for vibe coded three.js roguelite number 100002141/10124051202?  
Probably not.

Is there an audience for your play tested game with clear direction and vision for gameplay? Maybe? But even before AI lowered the barrier for entry they were still the minority.

replies.author: broncos4thewin
replies.body: I really don’t know this world at all but I guess there’s going to be a lot of slop out there and hopefully my game isn’t that. I just wondered if there was a “filter” which means AI stuff just gets completely ignored. I feel like the worst thing you can do is pretend your game isn’t AI.

comments.author: GlobalCurry
comments.body: If it's good people will probably play it. The AI hate can't last for long because everything is going to have AI somewhere in the development pipeline in the next few years.

replies.author: GlobalCurry
replies.body: Should add that what gets hate is generally one shot prompt games and clones that don't bring anything original.

comments.body:
Good stuff ? Yeah..

comments.author: Sunknowned
comments.body: Don't let the AI hate stop you. Doing it for fun is the best way. The ai slop code will become better as a time pass and models become stronger. The thing is - in near future ai models will be able to quickly refactor all your codebase to be more professional and optimized, specialized models will become better with media generation. Frontier models already can decompose and rewrite the full apps (adobe apps and ms office clones already exist rewritten in rust) so the future is hopefully bright.

comments.author: RemarkableWish2508
comments.body: There is an audience for working and fun games. You don't need to know the "scene", but you do need to know some game design, project management, and storytelling.

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: Retro point and click games have one of the smallest audiences in the industry and then you lose a certain number of people making it in AI, but you might get some players on itch.io, and some who will call it slop. Just make the game you want to make, don't do it for the money. Finding an audience is the hardest thing in games now, ai or otherwise

comments.author: Significant-Neck-520
comments.body:
I think there is an audience, yes, but the problem is that the algorithms detect the hate as the game being bad, and may not deliver to the target audience. 
For instance, say that 70% of players dislike AI, with about 10-20% hating it with a passion. It still leaves 30% as an target audience, but you will get the hate on many instances when trying to market your game, and it becomes an uphill battle. Many communities are pressured to ban AI content, for instance.
Also, I dont think steam has this figured out, but I'm not on steam.
The way I'm approaching this is that you loose about 2/3 of the audience but can produce something at 5 times the pace (realistically some parts change from months of work into a couple of days, while others don’t change at all), so if you charge less for your product, it can be made competitive.
In my experience, I could release my full game for free in itch.io and no one would care. Have less than 100 browser plays, took me a few weeks to produce.

comments.author: DoctaRoboto
comments.body:
There is an audience for this; don't listen to the AI haters. I am one of them; give me a badass, scary retro FMV movie in the style of 90s anime like Wicked City or movies like Hellraiser, and you've got a customer. Consumers, or what we call "tourists" or "normies," don't give a shit about AI. Do you think they know the names of the directors of the TV shows or movies they consume daily?

I always post the same on this forum: if you make something good, it will be succesful no matter how you did it. AI is being mocked and failing because...the products are SHIT. Look at the millions of fruit family videos infesting YouTube or those pathetic Dhar Mann rippoffs...no wonder AI-generated videos are called slob. The moment someone makes an AI movie at the level of Saw or Evil Dead...the tides will turn. Same with video games: what we got developed with AI? Mainly shitty porn FMVs or "visual novels" and some poor attempts at roguelikes, mainly crap.

The moment a lucky AI-game dev opens the flood gates...shit will start to change...very fast.

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body: There is, but in my experience it's not "people who like AI." It's people who like a specific kind of game, and the AI part is just how you got there. Lead with what the game is (a tactics RPG, a cozy sim, whatever) and mention the AI second. The hate mostly shows up when the post is about the tools instead of the thing you made.

comments.author: gcube2000
comments.body: The problem isn’t AI hate. The problem is AI is going to over saturate the market (if it hasn’t already).

comments.author: HamishGosling
comments.body:
Hmm, so the AI hate is very real and also very understandable. The nuance for me is whether a human is orchestrating the model and driving the 'taste' of the product, or if taste is being outsourced to AI. 

The reality is AI is being used to build everything, but that doesn't mean everything is slop inherently. But also, the vast majority of solo dev made products are AI slop and it feels like not many people building with AI at the moment have good taste. 

The models right now do not have a good sense of what a good human experience is - and actually this makes sense cause as a dev I've realised that my first instincts are also often bad and it's not until I use my products that I develop the taste that I think is actually good.

Not sure if that makes sense. Short answer is: there is demand for good products irrespective of whether AI was used to develop it, but only if the product has actual value. 

That said, because AI slop vastly outnumbers thoughtfully built products, most people's instinct is to reject products that they know are made using AI.
